📬 New shows added — 19 August 2026
==================================================

I added 4 new shows to The Safe Screen Time Database this week:

🟢 Wonder Pets! — Ages 2–4 — Low stimulation
   Available on: Nick Jr., Paramount+
   Common Sense Media notes the action 'moves along at a nice pace' with sweet, non-cloying songs and only 'very mild peril' when the trio rescues a new baby animal each episode; sung mini-opera dialogue and photo-collage animation keep it gentle. Rated from reviews, not scene-timed.

🟡 Between the Lions — Ages 4–7 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: PBS Kids
   A Sesame-style magazine format (puppetry, animation, live action) for ages 4-7 that packs many short reading segments, songs and wordplay skits into each episode, driving high novelty at a moderate tempo with low emotional stakes. Rated from PBS/reviews, not scene-timed.

🟡 Maya the Bee — Ages 3–6 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: Netflix
   Common Sense Media calls this CGI meadow show 'slow and easygoing' with 'mild' conflicts and only light menace, while new insect encounters and nature facts add some novelty against a bright, cheerful palette. Rated from reviews, not scene-timed.

🔴 Beyblade Burst — Ages 6–11 — High stimulation
   Available on: Disney XD, Netflix
   A competitive spinning-top battle anime (Common Sense Media: parents 8+, kids 6+) built on high-stakes tournament rivalries, rapid-cut battle sequences, and loud, flashy 'Let it rip!' effects with dramatic music. Rated from reviews and genre norms, not scene-timed.

📬 New shows added — 12 August 2026
==================================================

I added 10 new shows to The Safe Screen Time Database this week:

🟡 Gigantosaurus — Ages 3–6 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: Disney Junior, DisneyNOW, Netflix
   CGI preschool dino-adventure with recurring musical frolic sequences and bright, saturated visuals; reviews (Forbes, Common Sense) describe teamwork-driven stories with moderate action energy rather than frantic pacing. Cut speed and pacing estimated from general viewing, not scene-timed.

🔴 Ben 10 (2016) — Ages 6–11 — High stimulation
   Available on: Cartoon Network, HBO Max
   Reboot reviews note the 'bad guys come fast and furious' with a bright palette, rapid alien transformations, and comedy-forward but high-energy action; loud, dense sensory load. High-end factors inferred from reviews, not independently scene-timed.

🟡 The Smurfs (2021) — Ages 4–8 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: Nickelodeon
   Common Sense Media's review states this reboot has 'more action, more perilous moments, and less character build-up than the original,' citing chases, cliff falls, and exploding potions - a moderate step up in emotional spikes and pace from the 1980s series.

🟢 Trotro — Ages 2–4 — Low stimulation
   Available on: YouTube, France 5
   Repeatedly listed among low-stimulation toddler shows: gentle, slow, natural-language storytelling built around everyday routines of a little donkey, with calm visuals and quiet audio. Rated from those descriptions, not scene-timed.

🟡 Do, Re & Mi — Ages 2–5 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: Amazon Prime Video, Amazon Kids+
   Song-driven preschool series (KidsFirst/Common Sense) that explicitly teaches music concepts like tempo and dynamics; multiple songs per episode add sensory density but the overall rhythm is gentle and unhurried. Rated from reviews, not independently verified.

🟡 Sooty (2011) — Ages 4–8 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: CITV, ITVX
   Live puppet slapstick built around water pranks, magic mishaps and 'playful chaos' per series descriptions; single-set staging keeps cuts moderate while the comic set-pieces give it a livelier tempo. Rated from reviews, not scene-timed.

🟡 Rev & Roll — Ages 3–6 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: Nick Jr., Pluto TV, Amazon Prime Video
   Common Sense Media describes it as 'a calm show ideal for young preschoolers not ready for TV with too much conflict,' with no scary content or perilous situations despite its vehicle-adventure premise - keeping emotional and pace scores low.

🟡 Pop Paper City — Ages 3–6 — Moderate stimulation
   Available on: Apple TV+, Milkshake!
   Vibrant paper-world preschool show that alternates gentle 3D adventures with live-action craft montages encouraging kids to make their own creations; colorful but low-conflict and unhurried. Rated from descriptions, pacing not independently verified.

🔴 Trolls: TrollsTopia — Ages 4–8 — High stimulation
   Available on: Hulu, Peacock
   Common Sense Media highlights 'great music' and 'lots of random silliness,' with catchy numbers in constantly changing musical styles and a bright, glittery, high-energy palette - a loud, dense, fast-feeling show. Cut-speed and pacing inferred from reviews, not scene-timed.

🟢 The InBESTigators — Ages 7–11 — Low stimulation
   Available on: Netflix, ABC ME
   Dialogue-driven Aussie mockumentary ('an Office for kids') where kid detectives solve low-stakes mysteries; talking-head format and gentle humor keep cuts, sensory load and emotional spikes modest. Rated from reviews, not scene-timed.
